story.conflict: A grandmother must challenge her son's financial deception without making her grandson responsible for her disappointment.
story.hook: Her son charged her twelve thousand dollars to keep her grandson out of boarding school. Then he asked her to help the boy pack.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF TOBY NEEDED A SAY
story.premise: A grandmother pays her son twelve thousand dollars to cancel her grandson's boarding-school place, then discovers that her payment funded his departure.
story.punchline: the bag wasn't bringing him home
story.script: Margaret found Toby folding his school uniform beside the weekend bag she kept for his visits. Paul told her to help pack; the school fees were paid, and Toby's train left Saturday. She reminded him what the money was for. He said Toby needed the opportunity, and she would never have helped if he'd told the truth. So he'd invented a cancellation charge and promised the boy would stay home. Margaret demanded her money back. Paul said it was already gone, then called Toby downstairs to explain how much he wanted to go. The boy stopped at the doorway. His father had told him Grandma was paying because she supported him. Now he thought he had to choose between thanking her and disappointing her. Margaret put down the shirt she was holding and asked what he wanted when neither adult was answering for him. Toby wanted the science classes. He also wanted somewhere he wasn't listening to his parents fight every night. Paul started explaining that all couples argued. Margaret stopped him. Toby wasn't being asked to defend that either. She told Paul they still had twelve thousand dollars to discuss. Then she sat beside her grandson and asked when families could visit. He pushed the weekend bag toward her, worried she'd want it back. She put his folded shirt inside. This time, the bag wasn't bringing him home.
story.twist: The grandson wants to attend the school, and his father used the grandmother's opposition to obtain the fees she would otherwise have refused.

youtube.description: A grandmother pays to keep her grandson close, then discovers that neither adult has asked what he wants.
youtube.title: The Weekend Bag Beside His School Uniform

story.conflict: A bride must decide what to do when her groom treats his brother as a substitute for participating in their wedding.
story.hook: A groom asked his twin to take his place at the altar. He said he'd be back before the kiss.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF VOWS REQUIRE BOTH PEOPLE
story.premise: A groom asks his identical twin to stand in at the altar while he attends a promotion interview, promising to return before the wedding kiss.
story.punchline: She kept her ring in its box.
story.script: Oliver had borrowed his brother's jacket and watch for photographs while Ben took a video interview upstairs. Then Ben called and told him to start the ceremony. The bride, Lucy, was already waiting outside. Oliver said photographs were one thing. He wasn't going to make someone else's vows. Ben insisted they looked identical and nobody would know until he returned. Oliver walked straight to Lucy and handed her the phone. Ben told her this promotion could pay for their future. She asked why he hadn't requested another interview time. He admitted he'd kept the appointment because he didn't want to look difficult. But apparently asking his brother to marry her was easier. Lucy told Oliver to take off the watch. Then she went inside and told the guests there would be drinks, but no ceremony yet. Ben called again, annoyed that she'd made the delay public. He suggested Oliver could do the entrance while they saved the real vows for later. Lucy asked which other parts of their marriage he planned to attend himself. He finally closed his laptop and came downstairs. By then, the guests had left their seats. Ben asked whether they could hurry through it before anyone ordered food. Lucy said she needed a conversation before she could make a promise. She gave him his watch. She kept her ring in its box.
story.twist: The brother agreed to stand in for photographs, but refuses when the groom extends the request to the actual ceremony.

youtube.description: A groom's interview runs into his wedding, and his identical twin is asked to cover more than the photographs.
youtube.title: The Brother Wearing the Groom's Watch

story.conflict: Two customers must respond when a salesman treats one person's property and the other's payment as leverage to force another sale.
story.hook: Dan found a stranger buckling a child into his car at the dealership. A salesman had sold it while Dan was test-driving another one.
story.premise: A dealership sells a customer's car while he is test-driving another vehicle, then pressures him to buy the replacement to avoid disrupting the completed sale.
story.punchline: this time they were being offered a lift
story.script: Dan pointed to his son's schoolbag on the back seat. The woman, Beth, said she'd just paid for the car. The salesman hurried over and announced that Dan's trade-in was complete. Dan had only asked what it was worth. He'd left the keys so staff could move it while he tried another vehicle. The salesman said the misunderstanding was easy to fix: Dan could buy the newer car, and everybody could leave happy. Dan said he wasn't buying anything. Beth asked for her money back. The salesman told her refunds took several days, then warned Dan that taking the car would leave a mother and child stranded. Beth turned on him. He'd sold her a car that wasn't his, and now she was supposed to help him pressure its owner. She unbuckled her daughter and started removing their child seat. Dan reached for it. Beth stiffened, thinking he wanted her to hurry. Instead, he asked where they needed to go. She had to get home before her evening shift. Dan said he'd collect his son, then drive them home. The salesman offered another discount if they'd both stop making a scene. Beth put the keys in Dan's hand and held out her empty palm to the salesman. She still wanted her money. Her daughter asked whether they were getting back in the car. Beth said yes, but this time they were being offered a lift.
story.twist: The buyer refuses to keep the car once she learns the owner never agreed to trade it in, despite needing transport herself.

youtube.description: A test drive leaves two customers fighting over one car until they discover who created the problem.
youtube.title: The Child Seat in His Unsold Car

story.conflict: A tenant who needs affordable housing must refuse a grieving landlady's deception without treating her grief as a joke.
story.hook: A landlady admitted she'd been texting her mother as her dead son. Now she wanted her tenant to be his voice on a birthday call.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF HER OWN VOICE MATTERED
story.premise: A landlady who has been texting her mother as her dead son offers a tenant discounted rent to impersonate him on a birthday call.
story.punchline: she crossed out Grandma and wrote Mum
story.script: Rachel offered four hundred dollars off the rent. Ben needed the room, but asked how a stranger could possibly sound like her son. She said her mother hadn't heard Adam's voice for years. The messages had worked for six months. She pushed a birthday card across the table, with Grandma written on the envelope, and said the call only needed to last a minute. Ben agreed to try. Rachel dialed, then left him alone so he wouldn't feel watched. He managed hello. The woman immediately asked whether he was the young man renting Adam's room. Ben went quiet. She said a relative had told her about the death after the funeral. She knew who was really sending those messages. Ben asked why she hadn't said anything. She was afraid Rachel would stop writing altogether. Then she asked him to put her daughter on. Rachel came back ready to coach him. Ben covered the phone and told her he couldn't be Adam, even for cheaper rent. She reached to end the call. He said her mother knew, and still wanted to speak to her. Rachel sat down. She stared at the card before telling her mother happy birthday in her own voice. Ben offered to leave them alone again. Rachel stopped him long enough to say the room was still his at the lower rent. Then she crossed out Grandma and wrote Mum.
story.twist: The grandmother already knows her grandson died and has been answering the messages because she fears losing contact with her daughter too.

youtube.description: A discounted room comes with a request to make a birthday call in someone else's voice.
youtube.title: The Birthday Card That Came With Cheaper Rent
